historical_reviews.deepseek: The agent cannot install CPUs, but classifying the whole case NO discards automatable observation and evidence collection.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly separates manual hardware manipulation from automatable monitoring and recovery validation.

historical_reviews.v3_1: Requires a negative-boot oracle with a deadline and independent BMC reachability so 'will not boot' is distinguished from hang, power fault or management loss.

original_test_intent: Verify that a specified unsupported CPU population is rejected, produces the expected BMC and UEFI fault records, identifies the affected socket through lightpath, asserts the system fault indicator, and recovers after supported CPUs are restored.
original_method: A qualified technician installs an approved unsupported pair under power/ESD controls; automation observes power and boot milestones through an independent BMC path, captures indicators and logs, then the technician restores the supported population and automation validates UEFI SEL plus full health.
manual_activity: Qualified technician powers down, applies ESD controls, installs the approved unsupported CPUs, later restores the mapped supported pair and inspects physical lightpath/fault indicators where no reliable telemetry exists.
required_inputs: Unsupported CPU part number and stepping
Expected BMC/UEFI event IDs and socket mapping
safety_requirements: Agent never performs physical CPU work
Qualified technician follows power discharge, ESD, torque and thermal-interface controls
Verify unsupported parts do not exceed electrical/mechanical limits
Preserve baseline logs instead of clearing them
Stop on abnormal heat, smell, current or wrong-socket event
Do not repeatedly power-cycle a no-boot system
Restore supported CPUs before UEFI SEL validation
agent_execution_scope: Capture baseline inventory, firmware, logs and health
Guide but never perform technician-only swap
Observe BMC power, POST and boot milestones
Collect BMC event and indicator telemetry
After manual restoration collect UEFI SEL
Verify supported inventory, thermals and health
engineer_actions: Approve unsupported and recovery CPU populations
Define boot timeout and expected fault signature

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The narrative correctly blocks agent-performed CPU swapping but provides no commands for the automatable BMC/boot/SEL portions and no objective no-boot deadline.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Automate only read-only baseline/OOB inventory, boot-progress monitoring, timestamped event collection and post-restoration health checks around a qualified technician's physical swap; never automate power cycling beyond the approved single attempt.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Unsupported same-type CPUs, boot attempt, BMC web/UEFI SEL checks, indicators and 20/10-minute timing are preserved; exact parts, sockets and timeout are not guessed.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a two-operator handoff checklist with barcode/part capture, socket photos, independent OOB event timeline, POST/boot deadline, physical-indicator photos and a signed recovery health report.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the negative boot outcome measurable and separates manual hardware custody from automated evidence.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Distinguishes intended unsupported-CPU rejection from unrelated no-power, POST hang, BMC loss or technician installation error.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: BMC may remain available while host POST stops; UEFI SEL can only be checked after supported hardware is restored, so event correlation needs timestamps and socket identity.

project_override_considerations: 'Unsupported CPUs of the same type' is insufficient for execution. The unsupported dimension must be a documented part/stepping/platform-compatibility fact, not an arbitrary CPU that may be electrically unsafe.
expected_evidence: BMC inventory and exact event records
No hardware PASS claim by the agent

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and criteria consistently describe intentional unsupported-CPU rejection, indicators and logs. Exact unsupported parts and boot deadline are missing project inputs, not contradictory intent.

blocked_analysis.analysis: A qualified lab, approved parts, observer and recovery pair are finite packages. If unavailable after request, execution becomes blocked, but static review is complete.

review_improvement: Retains the operator-only physical boundary while recovering automatable OOB evidence and preventing an arbitrary no-boot condition from being misclassified as correct rejection.
independent_technical_reasoning: A negative boot result is ambiguous unless the platform reaches a defined rejection stage and emits the expected CPU/socket fault while management remains observable. The physical swap cannot be delegated, but telemetry collection and post-recovery correlation can. Exact unsupported parts and a known-good recovery pair control the hardware risk, making this a partial REQUIRES case rather than MANUAL ONLY.
